analysis.answer_text: Alright, let’s walk through a quick sequence to steady that connection.First, put your router in a central, open spot and away from things like microwaves, baby monitors, or thick walls that can block the signal.
analysis.reply_text: Good point—let’s handle that first so you can still move forward.First, check the router itself for a sticker with the default username and password, often on the bottom or back. Next, if your provider gave you an app, open it and look for a “manage Wi‑Fi” option that shows or resets the credentials. If that doesn’t work, try the default login printed on the sticker—many routers use something like “admin” for the username—and then create a new password right away if you can. If you’re completely locked out, use the router’s reset button, usually a tiny recessed pinhole, to restore factory settings, then log in with the default credentials. After that, set a strong new admin password and a strong Wi‑Fi password, and save them somewhere safe. Then reconnect your devices and test for stability. If it still drops, contact your internet provider, because the line or the router itself may need attention.
